simple: How many of the attempted deliveries really ended at the right place.
analogy: The parcels that reached the right door, counted by the customer, not by the courier.
precise: The number of task runs, out of a fixed number set in advance, in which every stop was reached within the task tolerance as measured by an independent reference (ground truth in simulation, a measured mark on the floor on hardware), with no collision and within the time limit; MP6 handbook definition.
source: C1 and R2 of MP6 (pending verification)

simple: On average, how far the robot's belief about its position was from where it really was.
analogy: How far the dot on your phone's map was from where you actually stood, averaged over the whole ride.
precise: In MP6, the root mean square of the distance between the estimated and the true position, sampled every 0.5 s after the first 5 s of a run, in the map frame; estimate and truth share the frame, so no alignment step is needed; MP6 handbook definition, after the RMS error of F9-34.
source: R1 and R9 of MP6 (pending verification)

simple: The fixed list of columns that every run's log has, whether it came from the simulator or the real robot.
analogy: The same delivery sheet used on the trainer and on the street, so the two can be laid side by side.
precise: A versioned contract that names each logged field, its unit, frame and rate; in the MP6 starter: t, leg, state, x_true, y_true, th_true, x_est, y_est, th_est, sd_x, sd_y, sd_th, v_cmd, w_cmd, v_true at 2 Hz, where the *_true fields come from the simulator or from an external reference on hardware.

simple: The same task with the same settings, run once in simulation and once on the real robot, so differences can be blamed on the robot and not on a changed setting.
analogy: Riding the same route on the trainer and on the street on the same day, with the same bicycle settings.
precise: Two runs that share the software version, configuration file, task, start pose and log schema, differing only in the plant (simulator or kit robot); the unit of the sim-to-real analysis of MP6 milestone M5; MP6 handbook definition.

simple: How far the robot still rolls after it is told to stop.
analogy: The length of road you need after squeezing the brakes.
precise: The distance the robot's reference point travels from the moment a stop is commanded until both wheels are still; for a drive that ramps each wheel down at constant deceleration a from speed v, the ramp alone gives v^2/(2a) per wheel, and reaction delays add their own distance.
source: W1 and R5 of MP6 (arithmetic, recomputed in the lab run)

simple: A deliberately planted fault that your tests did not notice.
analogy: A puncture the pre-ride check did not find.
precise: In mutation testing, a modified version of the program (in MP6 a removed safety mechanism or a wrong calibration value) for which every test still passes; it shows a property the suite does not check, and is either killed by a new test or recorded with a reason.
